title: Coding Agents
markdown:
Open Executive can dispatch **outbound** coding runtimes — Cursor CLI (`agent` / `cursor-agent`) and OpenCode — against operator-allowlisted repositories. This is the inverse of the **MCP Server** section: inbound MCP lets external agents consume OE; coding agents let OE consume a repo on the principal's behalf.

Coding runtimes are **not specialists**. They do not join `SPECIALIST_REGISTRY` or `consult_specialist`. They are Executive **tools** (like the MCP gateway or workflow starters): the model passes a `workspace_id` slug and a task; the API enqueues work and returns a `job_id` without blocking the chat turn.

## Module & config

Implementation lives in `openexecutive.coding_agents` (`service`, `store`, `tools`, `cursor_cli`, `opencode`, `file_config`, `models`, `audit`).

Enablement mirrors MCP: a non-empty, valid **`company/coding_agents.yaml`** (gitignored; template at `packages/core/coding_agents.yaml.example`) turns the feature on; explicit `CODING_AGENTS_ENABLED` overrides inference.

The YAML defines:

- **`workspaces`** — each entry has `id` (slug, never a path), `path` (on the **job host**), optional `default_runtime` (`cursor` | `opencode`).
- **`runtimes`** — per-backend `enabled`, optional `binary`, optional OpenCode `serve_url`.

The model must **never** supply a filesystem path — only `workspace_id` from this allowlist.

## Executive tools (always registered)

Three tools are sorted by name and **always** present on the Executive tool list so Anthropic prompt caching stays stable (disabled installs get structured errors from handlers):

| Tool | Role |
|---|---|
| `start_coding_job` | Enqueue ask/plan work; returns `job_id` immediately |
| `get_coding_job` | Poll status, events, and artifact when finished |
| `cancel_coding_job` | Cancel queued or running jobs |

When coding agents are enabled, **`CODING_AGENT_ADDENDUM`** (a constant in `executive_persona.py`, appended in `cache_manager.build_system_blocks` beside `MCP_ADDENDUM`) tells the Executive how to use these tools. Per-job output stays in tool results — not in cached system blocks.

User-facing replies must not name Cursor or OpenCode; audit/debug may.

## Modes & authority

| Mode | P1 |
|---|---|
| `ask` | Read/analyze allowlisted repo |
| `plan` | Propose a change without applying it |
| `agent` / `write` | **Refused** with `write_mode_deferred` (P2 adds authority + git worktree) |

Default runtime argv must not include `--force`, `--yolo`, or `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.

## Job lifecycle & persistence

Jobs persist in SQLite table **`coding_jobs`** on the episodic DB (`EPISODIC_DB_PATH`), same file as decisions and workflow state. `service.py` runs each job as an asyncio task; `store.update_job` uses compare-and-swap on status so a late success cannot overwrite cancel/timeout.

**Statuses:** `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`. Active work is `queued` + `running`.

When a job reaches `succeeded`, `failed`, or `timed_out`, the service inserts a principal-facing card on the same path as `draft_artifact`: `alerts` row with `source="artifact"` and `topic_tags=["artifact"]`, routed to the principal. That lands in `/today` **Needs you**. It does **not** DM. `cancelled` does not create a card. Title and body include `job_id`, the workspace **slug**, and status. Success cards include the artifact. Failure and timeout cards use fixed one-voice sentences (never runtime stderr, never Cursor or OpenCode names); operators inspect `GET /coding-jobs` for the log. Cancel compare-and-swaps to `cancelled` *before* abort so a kill-as-failure cannot persist `failed` and notify.

## Runtimes

**Cursor CLI (print mode):**

```
agent -p --trust --workspace <allowlisted-path> --sandbox enabled --mode ask|plan --output-format json "task"
```

Auth via `CURSOR_API_KEY` in an isolated subprocess env (not `--api-key` on argv).

**OpenCode:** when `serve_url` is set, HTTP `POST /session` binds the allowlisted workspace as `directory` (JSON body, plus `?directory=` and `x-opencode-directory` for current serve routing) and pins the read-only `plan` agent on both session create and `POST .../message` (same as CLI `--agent plan`). If serve cannot bind that directory (connect error, connect timeout, HTTP 4xx/5xx on session create, or a returned directory that does not match the allowlist), the job **fails closed** to CLI `opencode run --dir <path> --format json --agent plan "task"` rather than running against the serve process cwd. HTTP read timeouts after serve is reached fail the job as timed out rather than falling back. Without `serve_url`, CLI is used directly.

Subprocess env copies only `PATH`, `HOME`, `LANG`, `TERM`, plus runtime auth keys — not Slack, Google, or `BACKEND_SHARED_SECRET` wholesale.

## HTTP surface

Operator REST uses the same shared-secret gate as the rest of the API (`x-api-key` or `Authorization: Bearer`). Start stays on the chat tool `start_coding_job` — there is no `POST /coding-jobs`.

- `GET /coding-jobs` — list jobs (`status?`, `limit` 1–500)
- `GET /coding-jobs/{job_id}` — one job (404 if missing)
- `POST /coding-jobs/{job_id}/cancel` — cancel a queued/running job (404 if missing)

## Docker & topology

The default **`api`** container stores company data under `/data` only — **no git checkouts**, no Cursor/OpenCode binaries. Coding jobs must run where allowlisted repos exist (bare-metal dev host, or an optional worker/sidecar with bind-mounted repos and runtime credentials). See **MCP Server** for the inbound direction (Cursor/OpenCode as MCP *clients* of OE).
